## Table S10. Nested validation of the termination hazard model

(a) Out-of-sample performance of the adjustment-only model (log event age, day of the season, same-day national Tmin anomaly, winter start year) and of the model that adds the predictors selected within each training fold. In every fold, predictors were standardized with training data only, each of the 39 pre-outcome primary-family candidates was tested with a likelihood-ratio test, Benjamini–Hochberg q < 0.05 was applied, the diurnal temperature range was excluded (it is algebraically redundant with Tmax once Tmin is adjusted for), and candidates correlated at |r| > 0.8 with a stronger selected predictor were skipped. Folds are single winters with at least one spell (leave-one-winter-out) or the two halves of the record. ΔAUC and ΔBrier are the selected minus the adjustment-only model, with 95% winter-block bootstrap intervals; Brier skill is relative to the training-fold event frequency; the calibration slope and the ratio of observed to expected terminations refer to the held-out predictions. In the split-period folds the winter-start-year term is extrapolated beyond the training period; trained on the later half, even the adjustment-only model scores worse than the training-period climatology (compare the Brier columns), and calibration is poor in both directions. The risk set treats the two season-end spells as right-censored (83 terminations). (b) Predictors selected in the training folds. This table supersedes Table S7, in which the predictors had been chosen on the full record. The AUC values are plotted in Fig. S1b.

## Table S11. Sensitivity of the termination hazard model to the station network and to season boundaries

(a) The primary cold-night spell catalogue (26 stations) and the catalogue rebuilt on the 25 stations other than Satkhira, the station flagged by the homogeneity screen, with Voronoi weights recomputed. The rebuild code was first validated by reproducing the 26-station weights and all 85 primary spells exactly; the 84 rebuilt spells overlap 83 of the 85 primary spells (79 with identical dates). (b) Odds ratios of termination per standard deviation (95% winter-block bootstrap interval) for the 39 pre-outcome primary-family predictors, adjusted for log event age, day of the season, the same-day national Tmin anomaly and winter start year: as in Table S2 (primary), on the 25-station catalogue, with the two spells that end on the last day of the season counted as terminations instead of being right-censored, with the two spells that start on 1 December (whose age at the start of the season is unknown) removed, and with the final rows of the two censored spells omitted instead of coded as non-terminations (their outcome is decided by the Tmin of 1 March, outside the analysed season). ## Table S12. Termination hazard model with predictors taken one and two days earlier

(a) Odds ratios of termination per standard deviation with every predictor of the four families (primary; advection and jet; before the terminating night; terminating night) taken on day k − 1 instead of day k (predictor lag 1 day), adjusted for log event age, day of the season, the same-day national Tmin anomaly and winter start year. The adjustment still uses the Tmin of day k and the spell is ongoing on day k, so a lag describes older information, not a longer forecast lead. q is given within each family and for a single Benjamini–Hochberg correction across all 66 predictors. (b) 850-hPa advection and jet speed one and two days earlier, and the robustness of the one-day lag of advection over the northwestern Indo-Gangetic Plain (NW IGP) to counting the season-end spells as terminations, to the 25-station catalogue, to adding the same-day core predictors (10-m wind, South Asian Z500 tendency, T2m − T850 tendency, Tmax) and to adding same-day advection over both regions; only the one-day lag of panel (a) is part of the 66-predictor correction, and the intervals and p-values of panels (b) and (c) are nominal sensitivity results. At a one-day lag the terminating-night family describes the night before day k and is no longer concurrent with the outcome. (c) The NW IGP advection one and two days earlier refitted in each of the six alternative event catalogues (added after the pre-submission review); the minimum event age of the risk set is the shortest spell of each catalogue. Adv850 anomalies are relative to the calendar-day climatology; a positive anomaly means more warm or less cold advection than normal. Intervals are 95% winter-block bootstrap intervals (10,000 resamples). The NW IGP rows of panels (a) and (b) are plotted in Fig. 7c; panel (c) is not. One standard deviation corresponds to: Adv850, NW IGP 1.18 K day⁻¹.

## Table S13. Robustness of the deficit of cold-spell onsets after major sudden stratospheric warmings

Cold-spell onsets within each window after the 25 major SSWs of 1985/86–2024/25 (Table S1). Null rows compare the observed count with control dates moved to the same calendar date in randomly chosen other winters (calendar-matched) or in winters within five years of the SSW winter (decade-matched), 10,000 replicates each, redrawing any control date within 45 days of a real SSW (each SSW independently; the 100-attempt limit was never reached, Text S1). In these rows the ratio is a count ratio, observed over expected onsets, and the range is the 2.5–97.5 percentile range of the null distribution, not a confidence interval; two-sided Monte Carlo p-values are min{1, 2 min(p₋, p₊)}, with p₋ and p₊ the plus-one proportions of replicates at or below and at or above the observed count. The ratio per at-risk day divides onsets by at-risk winter days (days not inside an ongoing spell after its first day) in both the observed and the control windows. Onset-rate rows compare onsets per at-risk day after SSWs with all other at-risk DJF days, or with the rest of the winters that contain the SSWs; their ratio is a rate ratio with an exact conditional binomial 95% interval, which conditions on the counts and ignores dependence between onsets of the same winter. SSWs in March have no December–February follow-up. The ENSO-phase-matched null (6 onsets against 15.9 expected) is reported in the main text.

## Table S18. Station network

The 26 Bangladesh Meteorological Department stations of the fixed analysis network, each with at least 95% of December–February days observed in at least 38 of the 40 winters. Coordinates are those of the BMD station metadata. The area weight is the share of the national area in the station’s Voronoi (Thiessen) cell on a Bangladesh-centred Albers equal-area projection, clipped to the national boundary (geoBoundaries ADM0); the exact weights sum to 100% (the rounded values shown sum to 99.8%) and are archived in 02_metadata/step7d_primary_station_area_weights.csv. The homogeneity screen compares each station’s monthly Tmin residuals from the median of all other stations (Sect. 2.1); Satkhira, the only station with a signal (a 2.5-fold increase in residual variance after the 2022 source change), is excluded from the 25-station sensitivity catalogue (Table S11). Station data are not redistributed; the weights and network files are archived with the code.
